blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
British meetings look calm and polite. People speak in turn. Nobody shouts. Disagreements sound gentle.

But inside, decisions are made — usually quietly. Sometimes the decision is not even made in the meeting. A meeting starts with a minute of small talk. Then it moves through the agenda. Everyone can say something. At the end, someone says "let's take this offline." This means: we will sort it out in a smaller group later.

To be heard in a British meeting, speak clearly and stay calm. And agree before you disagree.

items.q: How do British meetings look on the outside?
items.why: "British meetings look calm and polite."

items.q: What does "let's take this offline" mean?
options: Sort it out in a smaller group later
items.why: "we will sort it out in a smaller group later."

items.q: What should you do to be heard in a British meeting?
items.why: "speak clearly and stay calm. And agree before you disagree."

items.q: The text suggests that the real decision…
options: is always made in the meeting
is sometimes made after the meeting
is made by the newest person
items.why: Inferência: "Sometimes the decision is not even made in the meeting."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which idea?
options: In British meetings, people speak in turn.
You should shout to win a British meeting.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz para ficar calmo e falar claro — gritar vai contra tudo isso.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver explicar a reunião de ontem para um novo colega. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, welcome to the team! You were in the Zoom meeting yesterday, right? Let me explain a few things.

You saw everyone was very calm and polite. Nobody said "no" in a strong way. When people disagree here, they do it gently. That is normal. Do not worry.

At the end, Sarah said "let's take this offline." I think you looked confused! It does not mean go offline on your computer. It means we will talk about it later, in a smaller group. Just three or four people. And they will make the real decision there, not in the big meeting.

One more tip. In British meetings, you get your turn to speak. Wait for it, stay calm, and speak clearly. And here is the important part: agree with something first, and then say your different idea. So you can say "yes, good point, and maybe we can also try this." People listen more when you do that.

Oh, and the meeting always starts with a minute of small talk — the weather, the weekend. That is normal too. Don't skip it!
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Where did Oliver and the new colleague meet yesterday?
items.why: "You were in the Zoom meeting yesterday, right?"

items.q: What does Oliver say "let's take this offline" means?
options: Talk about it later in a smaller group
items.why: "It means we will talk about it later, in a smaller group."

items.q: What tip does Oliver give for speaking?
options: Agree first, then say your different idea
items.why: "agree with something first, and then say your different idea."

items.q: The new colleague probably felt confused because…
options: he did not know what "take this offline" meant
items.why: Inferência: Oliver diz "I think you looked confused!" logo depois de explicar a frase.

items.q: What can we learn about small talk from Oliver?
options: It is only for the boss
It is a waste of time
It is normal and you should not skip it
items.why: Inferência: "That is normal too. Don't skip it!"

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Let's take this offline and talk after lunch." This means…
options: sort it out later in a smaller group
items.why: To take offline = resolver depois, num grupo menor.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Please look at the ___ before the meeting. It lists all the topics."
items.why: Agenda = pauta, a lista de tópicos da reunião.

items.q: "He stayed calm and did not get angry." Calm means…
items.why: Calm = calmo, tranquilo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "In British meetings, everyone must ___ — you wait for your moment."
items.why: To speak in turn = falar na sua vez, esperando o momento.

items.q: "There was a small disagreement, but it was polite." A disagreement is…
options: a moment when people do not think the same
items.why: Disagreement = discordância, quando as pessoas pensam diferente.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We can sort out the problem after the meeting." To sort out means to…
items.why: To sort out = resolver, dar um jeito.

items.q: "The boss needs to sign off on the plan first." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "Let's follow up on this next week." To follow up means to…
items.why: Follow up = retomar, dar continuidade depois.

items.q: "Two people pushed back on the idea, but politely." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar.

items.q: "We will roll out the new plan next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = colocar em prática, lançar.
